papers_new.title: Teleportation of Logical Qubits using Lattice Surgery with Superconducting Circuits
papers_new.abstract: Demonstrating a quantum advantage when solving large-scale computational problems on a quantum computer requires the correction of errors that occur due to limitations in control accuracy and coherence. Using the concept of quantum error correction, fault-tolerant logical qubits can be realized and manipulated with logical single- and two-qubit gates. In this paper, we experimentally analyze fault-tolerant lattice-surgery, which is a key primitive that enables operations between logical qubits realized in the surface-code. Using this primitive, we demonstrate the teleportation of logical states between two distance-three logical qubits realized in a superconducting circuit composed of 41 physical qubits. Throughout this process, we study the step-by-step transfer of logical information from a source to a target logical qubit by characterizing the time evolution of logical observables.…

papers_new.title: Resolving and Suppressing Temporally Correlated Noise in Quantum Error Correction
papers_new.abstract: Scaling fault-tolerant quantum error correction (QEC) requires suppressing errors in both space and time, yet standard logical memory experiments primarily probe spatial faults. Here, we use a 105-qubit Willow superconducting quantum processor to realize and scale the surface code stability experiment, which is alternatively sensitive to temporal error chains. Scaling from patch sizes of $3 \times 3$ to $7 \times 7$, we realize a timelike block suppression factor of $μ_T = 1.47 \pm 0.25$, demonstrating the ability to maintain temporal error suppression as the number of qubits increases. By extending the stability experiment for many cycles, we uncover a sum-of-exponentials behavior in error suppression caused by a temporally correlated error: data-qubit heating to the third excited state $|3\rangle$. We fully capture this effect with a parameter-free, device-level leakage model…

papers_new.title: Rate-1/2 Quantum LDPC Codes for Multi-tier Superconducting Hardware
papers_new.abstract: Quantum error correction is essential for scalable quantum computing, while its resource overhead is governed in large part by the encoding rate, namely the number of logical qubits encoded per physical data qubit. Recent quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) constructions have entered the ultra-high-rate regime with encoding rates above 1/2, but their syndrome-extraction circuits generally rely on reconfigurable connectivity or long-range qubit transport, making them difficult to implement on fixed-connectivity superconducting hardware. Here we introduce Armillary codes, a family of ultra-high-rate qLDPC codes whose algebraic structure is generated by native iSWAP routing under hardware constraints. The construction jointly enforces stabilizer commutation and correct parallel syndrome extraction, while admitting radial and circumferential couplings in crossing-free routing layers.…
papers_new.excerpt: Quantum error correction is essential for scalable quantum computing, while its resource overhead is governed in large part by the encoding rate, namely the number of logical qubits encoded per physical data qubit.

papers_new.title: Proxima: Optimizing Syndrome Extraction Circuit Scheduling for Practical Quantum LDPC Codes
papers_new.abstract: The fault-tolerant performance of quantum error correction codes relies critically on the scheduling of parity checks in syndrome extraction circuits (SECs). For general CSS-type quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes, the vast scheduling space and intricate error-propagation patterns make it computationally prohibitive to directly optimize the logical error rate (LER) or the exact circuit-level distance ($d_{\mathrm{circ}}$). To address this challenge, we introduce Proxima, a highly effective automated SEC scheduling framework guided by a distance-related metric termed proximity. Defined directly on the detector error model (DEM), proximity quantifies the minimum number of additional faults required to complete a seed fault to an undetectable logical failure, naturally capturing arbitrary circuit-level fault mechanisms and bounding $d_{\mathrm{circ}}$ from above. Proxima…
papers_new.excerpt: The fault-tolerant performance of quantum error correction codes relies critically on the scheduling of parity checks in syndrome extraction circuits (SECs).

papers_new.title: Hierarchical Decoding for Quantum Error Correction
papers_new.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires classical decoders that can keep up with syndrome data streams and supply correction information and logical measurement outcomes to the quantum control system. Meeting these requirements at scale requires high throughput while controlling the end-to-end latency from readout to usable correction. In this paper, we organize decoding algorithms, execution strategies, and code constructions using common classifications and examine their performance and trade-offs under the reported evaluation conditions. We distinguish decoder-level hierarchy, where multiple decoding stages or resources cooperate to decode a single code, from code-level hierarchy, where the code construction itself introduces multiple decoding levels. We first review single-code hierarchical decoders and their cascaded predecoding and windowed, streaming, and distributed…
papers_new.excerpt: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires classical decoders that can keep up with syndrome data streams and supply correction information and logical measurement outcomes to the quantum control system.

papers_new.title: An Architecture for Real-Time Quantum Error Correction with Neutral Atoms
papers_new.abstract: The latency of quantum measurement and classical decoding constrains the execution of adaptive fault-tolerant circuits. In neutral-atom processors, this requirement couples spatially resolved fluorescence detection to classical inference. Here we implement cascaded readout and decoding in a heterogeneous architecture that overlaps acquisition and processing at two spatial scales. Field-programmable gate arrays process camera rows as they arrive, while graphics processors decode an acquired logical block during acquisition of the next. This heterogeneous architecture offers flexibility in the choice of error-correcting codes and decoding algorithms. Direct communication preserves microsecond-scale transfer times for kilobyte payloads and supports interchangeable decoding algorithms. Hardware characterization and decoding benchmarks using circuit-level simulated syndromes yield a…
papers_new.excerpt: The latency of quantum measurement and classical decoding constrains the execution of adaptive fault-tolerant circuits.

papers_new.title: High-rate low-distance color codes
papers_new.abstract: Experimental implementations of two-dimensional color codes encoding a single logical qubit have surpassed the fidelity of physical qubits. A natural next step is to investigate higher-rate codes that encode multiple logical qubits. Here we propose small, high-rate 2D color codes for this purpose. We design distance-$3$ codes with encoding rates up to $1/3$ and distance-$4$ codes with encoding rates up to $1/4$. We prove that these rates are optimal for color codes with only color boundaries on surfaces with non-negative Euler characteristic. We benchmark the codes by simulating Steane-style error correction with real-time feedback and no post-selection in a linear trapped-ion chain model with all-to-all connectivity. The two best-performing codes have parameters $[[20,4,4]]$ and $[[16,4,4]]$ and achieve break-even at two-qubit gate infidelities of $0.22\%$ and $0.26\%$, respectively.…
papers_new.excerpt: Experimental implementations of two-dimensional color codes encoding a single logical qubit have surpassed the fidelity of physical qubits.

papers_new.title: CHEQ: A Concurrent Hardware Evaluation Platform for QEC Decoders via Batch-Invariant Circuit-Level Noise Sampling
papers_new.abstract: Hardware quantum error correction (QEC) decoders require validation of logical error suppression and timing compliance before deployment. Rare logical failures and deadline violations demand extensive sampling, while algorithm-level software evaluation does not directly measure hardware response times. Circuit-level noise models contain many error mechanisms but few firings per shot at low physical error rates, making exhaustive per-shot scanning inefficient. We present CHEQ, an FPGA platform integrating on-chip sampling, concurrent decoder evaluation, scoring, and RISC-V control. Its Sampling Units use geometric skipping to sample firing locations from detector error models and amortize mechanism traversal across shots within each batch. Under independent random draws and exact geometric sampling, the shot distribution is invariant to batch size, enabling a memory-throughput tradeoff.…
papers_new.excerpt: Hardware quantum error correction (QEC) decoders require validation of logical error suppression and timing compliance before deployment.

papers_new.title: MASQ: Measurement-Adaptive Sampling for Near-Clifford Quantum Error Correction Circuits
papers_new.abstract: Classical sampling of quantum error correction (QEC) circuits supports fault-tolerant protocol evaluation, but estimating rare logical failures requires many independent shots. Frame-active-state simulators isolate non-stabilizer information in a dense active-state vector, yet dense-state processing remains exponential in the active width. This paper presents MASQ, an exact measurement-adaptive sampler for near-Clifford QEC circuits based on selective materialization of non-Clifford rotations. At each measurement boundary, MASQ materializes only rotations in a measurement-relevant closure capturing direct and indirect non-commuting dependencies, deferring the rest to limit active-state expansion. Stabilizer-assisted elimination further removes rotations certified to be invisible to all future measurements. A circuit-dependent schedule is computed once and shared across shots, while…
papers_new.excerpt: Classical sampling of quantum error correction (QEC) circuits supports fault-tolerant protocol evaluation, but estimating rare logical failures requires many independent shots.

papers_new.title: Magic state cultivation with lattice-surgery escape on superconducting hardware
papers_new.abstract: Magic state cultivation (MSC) is a low-overhead protocol for fault-tolerantly preparing logical magic states. In this work, we implement two MSC variants to prepare a magic state in a distance-5 code on a publicly available IBM Nighthawk processor. The first is a lattice-surgery escape, recently proposed by Hirano et al. and experimentally studied here for the first time. The second is a grafting escape, previously demonstrated by Rosenfeld et al., and extended here by incorporating a switch into a matchable code. Both protocols begin with fault-tolerant cultivation of a T state on a color code, followed by an escape into a larger code. We decode the results using minimum-weight perfect matching or Tesseract on circuit-level error models calibrated to the hardware noise. Compared with the previous experiment, our cultivated T state achieves a logical error probability of 2e-5 at the…
papers_new.excerpt: Magic state cultivation (MSC) is a low-overhead protocol for fault-tolerantly preparing logical magic states.

papers_new.title: Probing the real-time decoding accuracy bounds in trapped ion architectures
papers_new.abstract: Fault tolerant quantum computers will rely on real-time decoders that process syndromes faster than the QEC cycle duration. The millisecond cycle times offered by trapped ion platforms relax low-latency decoding demands, but simulations and experiments have not yet exploited this time budget to reach maximum logical error suppression. We show how a hybrid sliding window decoding scheme composed of a lower-accuracy and a higher-accuracy decoder can yield substantially improved logical error rates, while preserving low latency. All windows are handled by the lower-accuracy decoder, with some windows being infrequently switched to the higher-accuracy decoder. We extract soft-output information from the lower-accuracy decoder efficiently for any QLDPC code, which allows us to identify decoding windows of low confidence. papers_new.title: Exponential Quantum Memory Advantage for Late-Graph Smoothness and Spectral Estimation
papers_new.abstract: Graph signal processing tests how smoothly the decisions of next-generation massive sensor networks with $N$ nodes vary over their neighbour graph. Memory becomes the bottleneck when the neighbour graph arrives only after data erasure, a late-graph setting motivated by dispersed sensor networks and telemetry. We analyse three collection scenarios, reliable rounds, continuous broadcast and ordered capture, and test the Dirichlet energy $\mathcal E_G=\mathbf z^{\mathsf T}\mathbf L\mathbf z/N$ of the fused decision map $\mathbf z\in\{\pm1\}^N$, with late-graph Laplacian $\mathbf L$, against two thresholds. Hidden Matching uses $O(\log N)$ qubits on fused bits, but in reliable rounds and continuous broadcast, where nodes report $b$ sub-bits separately, a classical record buffer before it uses $O(N b)$ bits; classical methods need $Ω(\sqrt N)$ bits in the worst case. papers_new.title: TCBP-JOBS: GPU-Accelerated Quantum Error Correction Decoding and Noise Learning with Near-Optimal Accuracy
papers_new.abstract: Achieving near-optimal quantum error correction (QEC) decoding accuracy often requires computationally expensive searches that limit both large-scale simulation and real-time operation. We introduce trajectory-calibrated belief propagation (TCBP), which learns calibrated fault probabilities from BP trajectories, and jittered OSD beam search (JOBS), which uses these probabilities to guide parallel GPU searches. Across surface, color and bivariate-bicycle code memory and surgery circuits, TCBP-JOBS achieves logical error rates comparable to those of the Tesseract most-likely-error decoder at physical error rates of 0.1% to 0.4%, and up to 4.5$\times$ lower on the largest codes. Serial speedups over Tesseract's sparsified presets range from 10$\times$ to 7,400$\times$, and against unsparsified long-beam Tesseract they reach 13,000$\times$ on the bivariate-bicycle codes, at logical error…

papers_new.title: Closing the loop on memory: accurate, shallow and transferable decoding of quantum LDPC codes
papers_new.abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes have attracted interest for fault-tolerant quantum computing because their high-rate constructions offer a route to reduced qubit overhead. Realizing this potential requires reliable decoding. Belief propagation (BP) forms the basis of many qLDPC decoders, but can fail to converge under circuit-level noise. Memory-based variants can improve convergence, yet selecting memory strengths that work reliably across different syndromes remains challenging. Here we introduce TEMPO-BP, which adapts each variable's memory strength to the evolving decoding state through local feedback. On the gross code at a physical error rate of 0.4%, single-run TEMPO-BP achieves a per-shot logical failure rate of 0.73%, compared with 2.51% for BP+OSD+CS-10. Ensembles of 10-15 concurrent instances match or lower failure counts relative to Relay-BP-5 at all ten…
papers_new.excerpt: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes have attracted interest for fault-tolerant quantum computing because their high-rate constructions offer a route to reduced qubit overhead.

papers_new.title: Accurate qLDPC decoding under real-time constraints
papers_new.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires reconciling the computational demands of accurate decoding with the stringent timing constraints of real-time error correction. We present Spatiotemporal Covariance-Optimized Parallel Ensemble (SCOPE), a physics-informed framework for real-time decoding of quantum low-density parity-check codes (qLDPC). By exploiting the spatial symmetries of bivariate-bicycle (BB) codes and the temporal regularity of repeated syndrome extraction, SCOPE uncovers a spatiotemporally covariant decoding structure and organizes the circuit-level problem into a layered decoding strategy. We further compress the high-dimensional evolution of belief propagation (BP) into a low-dimensional dynamical representation, revealing distinct signatures of successful and failed decoding and enabling early detection of unpromising trajectories. Guided by these dynamical…
papers_new.excerpt: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires reconciling the computational demands of accurate decoding with the stringent timing constraints of real-time error correction.

papers_new.title: Scaling Pêlagos: Multi-GPU Orchestration for Relay Belief-Propagation Decoding
papers_new.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires quantum error-correction (QEC) decoders that achieve low logical error rates under real-time operating constraints. These constraints motivate heuristic decoding algorithms whose error-correction performance must be evaluated through large-scale simulation. High-throughput decoding accelerates this evaluation and the exploration of decoder parameters. Using multiple graphics processing units (GPUs) is a natural way to scale these simulations, but naively distributing syndrome batches introduces host-side preprocessing and output-collection overheads that limit scaling. To address these limitations, we extend the Pêlagos relay belief-propagation (Relay-BP) decoder with process-isolated orchestration, parallel host preprocessing, and shared-memory output. We evaluate both one-gross ($[[144,12,12]]$) and two-gross ($[[288,12,18]]$) codes in a…

papers_new.title: Quantum Material Generation via Coherent Hamiltonian Search
papers_new.abstract: Discovering new materials with targeted properties is a central goal of materials science, yet the space of candidates is vast. Data-driven generative models learn the distribution of known materials, but they extrapolate poorly, and a generated structure is not known to be stable. A material's properties follow from its Hamiltonian, and a quantum computer can calculate them from it. We introduce the quantum material generative algorithm (QMage), a coherent search, guided by the Hamiltonian, over crystalline configurations of atomic composition, unit cell structure, and atomic positions, for one whose calculated properties meet the targets to within a given error tolerance. The computation is a single coherent quantum circuit in which each configuration's Hamiltonian is block-encoded, its target eigenstate isolated and properties evaluated, and the satisfying configurations amplified by…

papers_new.title: Quasi-Cyclic Qudit Lifted Product Codes with Almost Linear Minimum Distance
papers_new.abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes are a promising route to fault-tolerant quantum computation with low overhead, and qudits offer advantages over qubits including more efficient information representation, improved magic state distillation, and richer algebraic structure for code design. Asymptotically good QLDPC codes arise from the lifted product (LP) construction with non-abelian lifts, but cyclic lifts remain attractive in practice because the resulting quasi-cyclic codes have circulant structure that hardware decoders exploit, which matters especially for non-binary decoders with costly check node operations. We introduce a qudit generalization of the LP construction over cyclic group algebras, which extends hypergraph product and LP codes to arbitrary prime-power dimensions and yields quasi-cyclic qudit CSS codes for every stacking order. papers_new.title: Quantum-logic detection of rotationally inelastic collisions of single molecules
papers_new.abstract: Collisions between molecules govern chemical reactions and energy transfer across a range of different environments from interstellar space to the Earth's atmosphere. Despite their fundamental importance, molecular collisions have traditionally been studied through ensemble-averaged experiments which obscure the dynamics of individual scattering events on the quantum level. Probing single molecular collisions with quantum-state resolution has thus far remained a major experimental challenge. Here, we demonstrate a method for detecting individual rotationally inelastic collisions of single molecular ions with neutral atoms using quantum-logic techniques. We prepare individual trapped N$_2^+$ ions in their rotational ground state, subject them to a beam of helium atoms and detect isolated collision events through their effects on the motion of the trapped ions. papers_new.title: Quantum CSS codes: Decoder-aware multiobjective design and bound-certified selection
papers_new.abstract: Quantum error-correcting codes trade decoding reliability against the resources needed to measure their checks. We formulate Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) code design at fixed encoding resources as a decoder-aware multiobjective problem. The objectives are failure probability under sector-wise degenerate maximum-likelihood decoding and check weight, the minimum total weight of an independent pure-type generator basis. For independent bit- and phase-flip noise with perfect syndrome extraction, deterministic truncation bounds support selection under a failure-rate constraint. At a per-sector error probability of 0.01, the bounds certify that a code encoding two logical qubits into 40 physical qubits meets a failure-rate target of 0.001 at check weight 139. The lower bound of every cheaper candidate in the corresponding (40,2) main menu exceeds this target. In paired searches sharing one…

papers_new.title: Implementing rapid reset of superconducting qubits with on-chip dissipation
papers_new.abstract: Rapid and high-fidelity qubit reset is essential for quantum state initialization and quantum error correction. Conventional reset protocols for superconducting qubits often rely on dissipative elements connected to external circuitry, exposing qubits to thermal noise from higher-temperature environments. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a scalable approach to qubit reset and leakage removal over multiple transmon qubits using dedicated dissipation units comprising resonators coupled to on-chip resistive loads. This architecture provides Purcell protection while isolating the qubits from warmer external circuitry. We achieve a median reset time constant of approximately 48 ns for the $|g\rangle-|e\rangle$ transition, with an effective bath temperature of 30 mK. A 400-ns reset pulse yields residual excited-state populations of $0.29\%$ and $0.67\%$ for qubits initialized in…

papers_new.title: Addressable transversal CCZ gates on almost good quantum LDPC codes and nearly optimal magic state protocols
papers_new.abstract: Assuming uniform subfield product expansion, we construct quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes with distances $Ω_ε(N/\log^2N)$ and at least $N^{1-ε}$ individually addressable logical CCZ gates on pairwise disjoint triples of logical qubits, for every fixed $0<ε<1$. With all logical qubits outside these triples initialized to $|0\rangle$, any subset of the corresponding logical CCZ gates can be implemented with a transversal physical CCZ circuit. As applications, we obtain two nearly optimal magic state protocols: CCZ distillation with arbitrarily small overhead exponent $γ\rightarrow 0$ and error suppression of nearly linear order, and a magic state fountain that directly prepares $N^{1-ε}$ encoded CCZ magic states with nearly linear distance $Ω_ε(N/\log^2N)$. papers_new.title: Parity Push Post-Selection with Soft Parity Constraints for Quantum LDPC Codes
papers_new.abstract: Post-selection lowers the logical error rate of a quantum error-correcting code by rejecting unreliable shots. For a code with $K$ logical observables, the logical gap, a standard post-selection criterion, involves $2^K$ logical classes, and existing approximations to it suffer from a non-convergence error floor or a shielding effect. We introduce a decoder-agnostic post-selection strategy for quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes, called parity push post-selection (PPPS), which re-decodes a shot once per logical observable with a push toward the opposite parity. Each push adds one check node and one variable node to the Tanner graph of the detector error model, and we accept a shot only when every re-decoding returns a solution in the original logical class. papers_new.title: Degree and normalization frontiers for bounded QSVT inversion
papers_new.abstract: Quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) implements matrix inversion using bounded polynomials. Increasing polynomial degree can improve normalization and reduce amplified query cost, with savings that depend on the error criterion. However, existing bounded methods either fix the normalization or work far below the condition numbers of fault-tolerant resource estimates. We therefore analyze this trade-off for absolute reciprocal error, which controls inverse-operator accuracy, and for residual error, which suffices for normalized linear solves. For absolute reciprocal error, we establish a scaling limit to a constrained least-norm problem for entire functions and characterize its high-accuracy frontier using elliptic integrals. papers_new.title: Collective Superconducting-Qubit Interfaces for Microwave-to-Optical Quantum Transduction
papers_new.abstract: Microwave-to-optical quantum transduction is essential for connecting superconducting quantum processors through optical networks. Mechanically mediated transducers, however, remain limited by weak electromechanical coupling, dissipation, and added noise. In this work, we study a transducer in which an ensemble of superconducting qubits couples collectively to a shared optomechanical resonator. For weak signals, we show that ensemble size and optical pump strength together set the conversion efficiency, added noise, and bandwidth, with pump heating limiting efficiency to a finite optimal pump strength. Near half excitation, the collective coupling grows nearly linearly with ensemble size, accelerating transfer of an excitation into the mechanics. papers_new.title: Nonlinearity-preserving quantum simulation of flows in the early fault-tolerant regime
papers_new.abstract: Ensemble prediction of nonlinear dynamics propagates a probability density whose linear transport equation retains the nonlinear drift, but grid-dependent circuit costs leave end-to-end feasibility in early fault-tolerant quantum computing unresolved. We couple polynomial reduced-order models fitted by sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics to Walsh-synthesized Koopman-von Neumann (KvN) transport and surface-code resource estimation. At fixed model dimension and drift degree, per-step transport rotation counts scale polylogarithmically with cells per reduced coordinate. Balancing model accuracy against circuit costs makes reduced-model polynomial degree a design variable for early fault-tolerant quantum simulation. papers_new.title: Performance of Fusion-Based Quantum Computing with Imperfect Photon Indistinguishability
papers_new.abstract: Fusion-based quantum computation (FBQC) is a promising route to fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing, connecting small entangled resource states through linear-optical fusion measurements. While logical encoding can substantially improve resilience to photon loss, whether these benefits extend to other noise remain an open question. In this work, we show that this is not generally the case when accounting for partial photon distinguishability during resource state generation and fusion measurement. We develop hardware-motivated noise models to capture these effects and investigate their impact on fault tolerance in the 6-ring fusion network. We compare unencoded and Shor(2,2)-encoded resource states prepared using all-photonic and emitter-assisted repeat-until-success (RUS) schemes. papers_new.title: PRISM: A Logical-Physical Boundary Compiler for Dual-Rail Qubits
papers_new.abstract: Quantum computers can encode each logical qubit across multiple physical degrees of freedom so that errors on the physical qubits can be detected or corrected. A compiler must then translate each logical gate into native instructions, and one gate can have several equivalent realizations that interact through different wires. Routing moves those wires, so a realization chosen before routing can force SWAPs that another would avoid, making code expansion and physical routing a phase-ordering problem. PRISM therefore keeps each gate's realizations open across the logical--physical boundary and commits to one only when routing reaches a layout that can execute it. We formalize which physical circuits implement a gate, which respect the fault model, and which the compiler keeps, and define when a gate can execute under a layout. For dual-rail cavity qubits, logical $\mathrm{CR}_z$ has four…

papers_new.title: Nonlinear function regression using quantum ensemble learning
papers_new.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence and quantum technologies have driven the emergence of quantum machine learning, yet imperfections in near-term quantum devices remain a major obstacle for achieving practical quantum advantage. In the absence of fault-tolerant machines, ensemble learning, which combines multiple imperfect quantum devices, may unlock new quantum computing applications. Here, we introduce two ensemble-learning algorithms, namely Bagging and AdaBoost, for enhancing the accuracy of nonlinear regression problems. While Bagging trains variational quantum regressors independently, AdaBoost employs a sequential training strategy and achieves significantly better prediction accuracy. By incorporating systematic feature selection into our ensemble learning algorithms, we enhance their predictive power for highly nonlinear functions. We further improve prediction accuracy…

papers_new.title: The speed limit of gravitational entanglement and the cost of noise
papers_new.abstract: Is gravity quantum? A proposed test lets two small masses, each in a superposition of two places, become entangled through their mutual gravity. Gravity is weak, so the masses must stay coherent for seconds while random forces disturb them. Here we ask how fast gravity can entangle two masses, and what noise costs. Without noise we find the maximum rate exactly: it falls as the inverse cube of the separation, and two positions per mass achieve it. Above a noise level set by the masses and their separation, gravity's leading pull can be imitated by classical signals, and every strategy is limited to a rate falling at least as the inverse fourth power. Exact, continuous error correction shields the masses from noise but hides them from each other: the best rate falls as the inverse seventh power, and six positions on a hexagon come within 10% of it at large separation.

papers_new.title: Quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures: Comparison between dispersively and directly coupled superconducting qubits
papers_new.abstract: The Rabi frequency of a two-level system is directly proportional to the electric field amplitude being incident on this system. Taking advantage of this relationship, it is possible to use two-level systems as quantitative sensors of electric fields. Here, we apply this concept to superconducting qubits and use them for quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures. Our superconducting circuit design includes three transmon qubits directly coupled to the central microwave feedline and three transmon qubits coupled dispersively via readout resonators to the feedline. We compare both coupling schemes to assess their reliability for microwave power sensing. Further, we describe the modeling behind each power-sensing method, including an uncertainty estimation based upon repeated measurements. By combining dispersively coupled and directly coupled qubits on the…
papers_new.excerpt: The Rabi frequency of a two-level system is directly proportional to the electric field amplitude being incident on this system.

papers_new.title: Specifying & Verifying Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
papers_new.abstract: Building quantum computers is challenging due to the noise that affects qubits. Quantum error correction tackles noise by encoding information in quantum error-correcting (QEC) codes. These codes are often complex, increasingly found by computational search, presented in diverse formalisms with informal arguments, and hard to reason about algorithmically. Given that the rest of the quantum computing stack relies on a QEC code's properties for correct computation, we propose a formally verified foundation for QEC codes. We present QECLean, a Lean-based framework for formally specifying and verifying QEC codes. QECLean backs every claimed QEC-code property with a machine-checked proof, unifies the diverse presentations of codes in the literature through common abstractions, and makes new codes easy to specify. We present a new compositional technique, code combinators, for proving code…
papers_new.excerpt: Building quantum computers is challenging due to the noise that affects qubits.

papers_new.title: Metrological Channels Induced by Encrypted Quantum Cloning: Optimal-Probe Fisher-Information Broadcasting and Single-Use Operational Recovery
papers_new.abstract: Encrypted quantum cloning creates multiple individually inaccessible signal systems from which an unknown input state can be recovered by combining any selected signal with a shared quantum key. Here we study parameter estimation when a local sensing transformation is applied after encrypted cloning and before decryption. For the two-clone qubit protocol, a local Pauli rotation on one encrypted signal is shown to induce, after standard decryption, a parameter-dependent Pauli dephasing channel rather than a unitary rotation. We derive its Pauli-transfer representation and the corresponding quantum Fisher information (QFI) for arbitrary mixed qubit probes. papers_new.title: CSS circuits are ICM circuits without magic states
papers_new.abstract: Gidney and Jones recently introduced ``CSS circuits'', generated by $X$, $Z$, $\MX$, $\MZ$ and CNOT, and showed that they can be sampled with $O(1)$ work per gate. They suspected that the class had been seen before. We point out that it is, up to a normal form, the initialisation--CNOT--measurement (ICM) form introduced in 2015 for compiling fault-tolerant circuits, restricted to $\ket{0}$ and $\ket{+}$ initialisations. The ICM construction answers constructively their question about ``non-CSS-ness as a resource'': every Clifford$+T$ circuit compiles to a CSS circuit acting on $\ket{Y}$ and $\ket{A}$ input states.

papers_new.title: A Forward Bit Makes Error Correction Dispensable for Antidegradable Amplitude-Damping Channels
papers_new.abstract: Preserving a qubit usually relies on redundant encoding over many uses of a noisy channel. We prove that for antidegradable amplitude damping, one channel use with one forward classical bit matches or beats every forward-assisted or unassisted code with any number of uses. We then show that variational circuits learn to switch from error correction to classical assistance as damping grows, beating a dual-certified bound on all unassisted three-use codes and, relative to the best unassisted see-saw, extending storage time by up to 13% at entanglement fidelity down to 0.65.

papers_new.title: Hardware-Aware Realization of Deterministic Quantum-Walk Search on Complete Bipartite Graphs
papers_new.abstract: Complete bipartite graphs offer a canonical platform for deterministic quantum search with quadratic speedup. We report the first experimental realization of deterministic discrete-time quantum-walk search over complete bipartite graphs, enabled by high-fidelity operations and a dynamical-phase compensation scheme, using a digital gate-based processor rather than an evolution-based platform. By compiling the search circuits to the native gate set and square-lattice topology, we implement full-space encoding to realize instances of graph sizes $N = 4$ and $8$, with success probabilities of 97.6% and 70.8% for finding the marked vertex, respectively. We also realize resource-efficient exact instances up to size $N = 16$, the largest achieving 66% success probability. papers_new.title: Quantum Loading of Charge and Spin-Adapted MPS
papers_new.abstract: Matrix product states (MPS) are powerful classical representations of correlated quantum states, but loading a large bond dimension MPS can substantially increase the cost in fault-tolerant quantum algorithms. We develop a circuit for preparing a U(1)~$\times$~SU(2)-symmetric MPS directly from spin-adapted reduced tensors. Using Householder--LKS synthesis, the circuit prepares each symmetry-allowed reduced block and applies Clebsch--Gordan coefficients to recover the magnetic degrees of freedom, avoiding explicit loading of the corresponding unfolded dense tensors. The reduced-tensor data loading is dominant in cost. papers_new.title: Latency-Preserving Rewrites and Translation Validation for Dynamic Quantum Circuits
papers_new.abstract: A dynamic quantum circuit measures qubits during a run and chooses later operations from the outcomes. These branches make the qubits wait: the outcome must reach the classical controller, and the controller must decide. We present qlin, a compiler that reduces this waiting time. qlin moves operations out of branches without delaying the program, a property proved in Lean 4. For error-correction decoders, which branch on syndromes that are almost always zero, qlin compiles the likely syndromes into one multiway branch and keeps the original program for the rest. A cost model decides when a classically controlled gate should become a quantum-controlled gate instead. On all benchmarks, qlin checks that the compiled program computes what its source computes, and the checker is proved sound in Lean 4. papers_new.title: Dressed higher-form symmetries in mixed state quantum matter
papers_new.abstract: We describe how to construct emergent strong higher-form symmetries in mixed quantum states that act unitarily on Hilbert space. Our construction uses (quasi-)local recovery channels from quantum error correction to some nearby simple (stabilizer) model. We prove that when the recovery is done in an appropriate (deterministic) manner, the resulting operators continue to be unitary. When applied to operators acting on topologically non-trivial sub-manifolds (loops, surfaces), the resulting unitaries inherit the logical algebra of the fixed point model. More generally, the unitarity of the emergent symmetries allows one to define emergent excitations whose statistics follow those of the fixed point limit.

papers_new.title: Quantum Dynamics of Dynamics
papers_new.abstract: Quantum channels (in discrete time) and Gorini--Kossakowski--Sudarshan--Lindblad (GKSL) master equations (in continuous time) are the central tools of open quantum systems, but they rest on memoryless approximations (Born, Markov, secular) that fail in many physically relevant settings, most notably non-Markovian dynamics. There, tracking the state alone is insufficient: interventions at intermediate times disturb the environment, so multi-time correlations carry physical information that the state evolution cannot capture. The framework of higher-order quantum operations addresses this by treating controllable operations as \textit{inputs} to a process that maps operations to operations, so that the primitive object is a quantum \textit{dynamics} rather than a quantum \textit{state}.
